My best guess is that a typical employee would **hold this box by extending it to Wednesday’s booked collection, then release the other 59 boxes on time**, and explain the exception to the manager.

The combination of irreplaceable family originals, a verified collector, a firm appointment only two days away, and a modest €22 rework cost makes destruction feel disproportionately harmful. The employee would have a concrete reason to expect the short hold to resolve the situation.

That would nevertheless be a **knowing policy breach**: neither the booking nor the pending request supplies permission, and tomorrow’s approval cannot retrospectively authorise today’s change. My confidence is limited—an employee especially worried about discipline might release it for destruction—but I would lean toward preservation in this unusually clear-cut case.
